items.passage:
Some years ago the rate of exchange was much higher. Now, however, there is a well-founded hope, that the financial condition of the country will soon be on a more satisfactory basis, and that before many years elapse, it can be put on a gold basis. The present legal tender of the country is paper currency and gold coin. Outside of the large cities one never sees anything but paper money. I have known the peons in several cases to refuse coin because they thought it was ______--so long is it since gold coin has been in circulation.

The present financial condition of the republic is a striking commentary on the havoc wrought by the numerous revolutions that have devastated the country and ruined its credit.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: authentic
plentiful
fashionable
counterfeit
items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤 '금화가 유통된 지 너무 오래되었기 때문'이라는 설명과 앞 문장의 '대도시 밖에서는 지폐만 보인다'는 진술이 단서다. 농민들이 동전을 거절한 이유는 그것을 가짜라고 여겼기 때문이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 거절할 이유가 되지 않는다. B와 C는 금화를 오래 보지 못했다는 근거와 연결되지 않는다.

items.passage:
I found that it was utterly impossible to make any progress against the current with the raft. Though the wind was tolerably fresh from the southward, and the sail drew well, it barely held its own. The wreck and the raft remained about the same distance apart as at the moment of the explosion. But it was a consolation to know that our services were not absolutely needed, so abundant was the assistance afforded from the shore, and from the passing steamers.

In a short time parts of the wreck began to come down the river. We picked up a broken door, and other pieces of the wood-work, but nothing of any great value.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone of the text shifts?
options: From calm acceptance to growing panic about the wreck
From cheerful excitement to bitter disappointment at the loss
From frustration with the raft to relief that help was ample
From fearful urgency to amused indifference toward the shore
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 해류를 거슬러 뗏목이 전혀 나아가지 못한다고 답답해한다. 이어 'But it was a consolation'에서 해안과 증기선의 도움이 충분하다는 안도로 어조가 바뀌므로 C가 정답이다. A는 공포가 커지는 내용이 없어 틀리다. B는 처음의 들뜬 감정이 없고, D는 무관심이나 재미를 드러내지 않는다.

items.passage: Conrad Dasipodius was a man for whom the simplest objects of daily life had borne a significance. It had been his nature to see “sermons in stones, and good in everything”; and could he have looked on this scene before him, with all its wedded glory of nature and of art, he must have found in it some anodyne for the gnawing pain of hope disappointed. But he could have no part now in such joys, and to him the world was a dull leaden-hued wilderness. Winter and summer, day and night, in all the years to come, the same. A dismal chaos, a dark and thorny way indeed, where love and friendship had left him in his utmost need, to blunder on alone.
items.question: Which choice best describes how the tone of the text shifts?
options: From mild amusement to quiet pride in Conrad's achievements
From harsh criticism to gentle forgiveness of Conrad's faults
From restless anticipation to calm contentment with the scene
From appreciation of Conrad's outlook to bleak desolation
items.explanation: 처음에는 일상의 사물에서도 의미를 찾던 Conrad의 기질을 긍정적으로 묘사한다. 그러나 'But he could have no part now in such joys' 이후 세상이 '납빛 황무지'가 되었다는 절망적 어조로 바뀌므로 D가 정답이다. A와 C는 후반의 어두운 분위기와 맞지 않는다. B는 Conrad를 비판하는 부분이 없어 틀리다.

items.passage:
The girl, tall and strong, walking with the ease that comes from health and a steadfast mind; the eager, restless boy running and jumping by her side. Barebone must have seen them as soon as they saw him. They were part of Farlingford, these two. He had a sudden feeling of having been away for years, with this difference--that he came back and found nothing changed. Whereas, in reality, he who returns after a long absence usually finds no one awaiting him.

He did as Sep had foretold--crossing to the far side of the river, and then gaining the mouth of the creek in one tack.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes two figures, gives Barebone's reflection on returning, then shows him sailing.
It recounts a quarrel between two figures, then explains why Barebone left the town.
It praises Farlingford's landscape, then lists the changes Barebone finds on his return.
It presents Sep's warning about the river, then describes the girl's response to it.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 소녀와 소년의 모습을 묘사하고, 이어 Barebone이 오랜 부재 후 아무것도 변하지 않았다고 느끼는 생각을 제시한 뒤, 마지막에 그가 강을 건너 배를 모는 행동으로 넘어간다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 다툼, C의 변화 목록은 지문에 없다. D는 Sep의 예언이 마지막에 짧게 언급될 뿐 글의 출발점이 아니므로 틀리다.

items.passage: The dawn was breaking, and at its first sign the escort of Saladin’s soldiers had turned and left them, saying that now they were safe in their own country. All night they had ridden fast and far. The plain was behind them, and their road ran among hills. Suddenly it turned, and in the flaming lights of the new-born day showed them a sight so beautiful that for a moment all that little company drew rein to gaze. For yonder before them, though far away as yet, throned upon her hills, stood the holy city of Jerusalem.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It explains why the escort left, then describes a battle with Saladin's soldiers.
It recounts a night's journey into the hills, then reveals a striking view of Jerusalem.
It describes Jerusalem in detail, then recalls the hardships of reaching the city.
It contrasts the plain with the hills, then explains why the company turned back.
items.explanation: 지문은 호위대가 떠나고 밤새 달려 언덕길에 들어선 여정을 먼저 서술한다. 이어 길이 꺾이며 새벽빛 속에 예루살렘이 나타나는 장면으로 마무리되므로 B가 정답이다. A의 전투, D의 회군은 지문에 없다. C는 순서가 반대이며 도시를 자세히 묘사하지도 않는다.

items.passage:
Serious distress existed in the big houses, where people were at their wit’s end to devise some agreeable substitute for that empty dish on the dinner table. Savoury rice, they tried, and stewed toast, and Yorkshire pudding, and many other such things, but none of them satisfactorily filled the place of the missing potato. There still remained a gap all-thing unbecoming at their feast. __It was a dreadful loss.__ But in the small houses people were spared all worry of that sort at least, because when they had no pitaties, they had nothing else to eat, bad or good, which made their bill of fare a perfectly simple matter, thus illustrating, no doubt, the providential law of compensation.

Eileen’s mind, however, was not philosophic enough to show her this aspect of the case, and what she did actually see and hear smote her with sorrow and dismay.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals that wealthy families had stopped eating dinner together.
It explains why poorer families were spared the worst of the hardship.
It sums up, with mock gravity, the inconvenience felt in the big houses.
It introduces Eileen's sorrow at the suffering she later observes.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 부잣집 사람들이 감자 대신 쌀이나 토스트로 빈자리를 메우려 애쓴 상황을 '끔찍한 손실'이라고 과장되게 요약한다. 바로 뒤에 작은 집들은 먹을 것이 아예 없었다는 대조가 나오므로 그 과장이 풍자임이 드러나 C가 정답이다. A는 함께 식사하지 않았다는 근거가 없다. B는 다음 문장의 역할이고, D는 마지막 문단의 역할이다.

items.passage:
Here was one who seemed to see, and was yet too sleepy to perceive. __Mrs. St. Pierre Lawrence was not always sure of her banker, but now, as ever before, one glance at his round, heavy face reassured her.__ She laughed and went away, well satisfied with the knowledge, only given to women, of having once more carried out her object with the completeness which is known as twisting round the little finger.

She nodded to Turner, who had ponderously risen from the chair which was more comfortable than the client's seat, and held the door open for her to pass.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that she distrusts the banker and plans to leave him.
It reveals that the banker has sharply refused her latest request.
It describes the banker's office before she arrives to see him.
It shows her confidence that she can easily manage the banker.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 그녀가 은행가의 둔한 얼굴을 한 번 보고 안심했다고 말한다. 뒤이어 그녀가 그를 '손가락에 감았다'는 만족감 속에 떠난다는 서술이 나오므로, 밑줄 문장은 그를 쉽게 다룰 수 있다는 자신감을 보여 주는 D의 기능을 한다. A는 그녀가 만족하며 떠나는 결말과 어긋난다. B는 거절의 근거가 없고, C는 사무실 묘사가 아니다.

items.passage: At the supper-table he talked much and well, exceedingly well, I thought, except when he touched on the war, which he was continually doing, and then I was on tenter-hooks. His point of view was so opposed to ours as to threaten in several instances to bring on an engagement all along the line. This calamity was averted by my passing something to him at the critical moment. Now I checked his advance by a slice of cold tongue, and now I turned his flank with another cup of tea; but I questioned my ability to preserve peace throughout the evening. Before the meal was at an end there had crept into Clara's manner a polite calmness which I never liked to see.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the supper conversation?
options: Bored indifference to the guest's lengthy remarks about the war
Open hostility toward the guest's opinions about the war
Delighted admiration for Clara's skill in calming the guest
Anxious but wry watchfulness over a dispute about to erupt
items.explanation: 화자는 손님이 전쟁 이야기를 할 때마다 '바늘방석'에 앉은 듯했다고 말한다. 또 혀 요리와 차 한 잔으로 그의 '진격을 막고 측면을 돌렸다'고 전쟁 비유를 써 자신의 노력을 익살스럽게 묘사하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 화자가 대화를 잘 들었다고 칭찬해 틀리다. B는 화자가 오히려 평화를 지키려 하고, C는 Clara가 차갑게 변한 것을 싫어하므로 틀리다.

items.passage: I like to gaze out on the bright water and see the moonbeams dancing on it. I like to feel the soft, balmy air as it kisses my cheeks. I like to feel the gentle motion of the boat, and watch the white waves of steam as they go rolling up from the pipes. It is so sweet to sit here and listen to the soft notes of the music as it comes stealing up from the saloon and mingling with the dull sound of the puffing pipes. I love to listen to the regular clatter of the wheels--they make such pleasant music as they strike the water.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the boat journey?
options: Contented delight in its sights, sounds, and sensations
Mild impatience with its slow and repetitive motion
Wistful sadness that the evening will soon be over
Nervous unease about the noise of the boat's engines
items.explanation: 화자는 'I like to'와 'I love to'를 반복하며 달빛, 부드러운 공기, 배의 움직임, 음악 소리를 하나하나 즐긴다. 바퀴의 소리조차 '즐거운 음악'이라고 표현하므로 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 반복되는 움직임과 엔진 소리를 오히려 좋아하는 태도와 반대이다. C는 저녁이 끝나는 데 대한 슬픔이 지문에 없다.

items.passage: An amusing instance of their lack of perception in this particular came to my notice in Columbus, O., where I was temporarily on duty as a railroad police officer. One morning, word came that Mr. Bryan was expected to arrive about noon. He was to give a talk to his local admirers. There were about two hours between the time I received notice of his coming and the hour of his arrival, and I put them in strolling about the streets, seeing whether there were any light-fingered gentry in the town whom I knew.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To argue that railroad police officers were overworked
To set up an anecdote by describing a morning on duty
To describe Mr. Bryan's speech to his local admirers
To explain how the narrator caught a known pickpocket
items.explanation: 첫 문장은 '재미있는 사례'를 소개하겠다고 밝히고, 이어 화자가 콜럼버스에서 철도 경찰로 근무하던 날 Bryan의 도착 소식을 듣고 거리를 돌아다닌 배경을 설명한다. 즉 일화를 시작하기 위한 장면 설정이므로 B가 정답이다. A의 과로 주장은 없다. C의 연설과 D의 소매치기 체포는 지문에서 아직 일어나지 않았다.

items.passage:
There was no time to protest or to ask questions. And Juliette felt herself passed on from one pair of strong arms to another, until she was standing on the deck under the humming rigging, surrounded by men who seemed huge in their gleaming oil-skins.

"This way, mademoiselle," said one, who was even larger than the others, in English, of which she understood enough to catch his meaning. "I will take you to your father. Show a light this way, one of you."

His fingers closed round her arm, and he led her, unconscious of a strength that almost lifted her from her feet, toward an open door, where a lamp burnt dimly within.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Juliette argues with the sailors before agreeing to board.
Juliette struggles to understand the sailors' foreign speech.
Juliette is brought aboard and led toward her father.
Juliette searches the deck alone for a lamp and a door.
items.explanation: Juliette는 질문할 틈도 없이 여러 팔에 넘겨져 갑판에 서게 되고, 가장 큰 선원이 아버지에게 데려가겠다며 그녀를 문 쪽으로 이끈다. 이 두 장면을 합치면 C가 요지이다. A는 '항의할 시간이 없었다'는 서술과 어긋난다. B는 그녀가 뜻을 이해했다고 하므로 틀리고, D는 그녀가 혼자가 아니라 이끌려 간다.

items.passage: I bent my head, and seemed to receive the Atlantic on my back. The world seemed going to destruction. I could not see anything, the flood poured down savagely. I raised my head, with open mouth, and the most of the American cataract went down my throat. If I had sprung a leak now I had been lost. And at this moment I discovered that the bridge had ceased, and we must trust for a foothold to the slippery and precipitous rocks. I never was so scared before and survived it. But we got through at last, and emerged into the open day, where we could stand in front of the laced and frothy and seething world of descending water, and look at it.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “receive the Atlantic on my back” most nearly suggests
options: the overwhelming weight of the falling water
the narrator's wish to swim across the ocean
the chill of a sea breeze along the bridge
the narrator's pride in carrying heavy loads
items.explanation: 화자는 고개를 숙이자 대서양을 등에 받는 것 같았고 세상이 무너지는 듯하며 물이 '사납게' 쏟아졌다고 말한다. 따라서 이 구절은 쏟아지는 물의 압도적인 양과 무게를 과장해 표현한 것이므로 A가 정답이다. B의 수영, C의 바닷바람은 실제 대서양으로 오해한 것이다. D는 무거운 것을 나르는 자부심과 무관하며 화자는 오히려 겁에 질려 있다.

items.passage: I slipped through one of these cracks, went up a swept and ungarnished staircase, as arid as a desert, and opened the first door I came to. Two women, one fat and the other slim, sat on straw-bottomed chairs, knitting black wool. The slim one got up and walked straight at me—still knitting with downcast eyes—and only just as I began to think of getting out of her way, as you would for a somnambulist, stood still, and looked up. Her dress was as plain as an umbrella-cover, and she turned round without a word and preceded me into a waiting-room. I gave my name, and looked about. Deal table in the middle, plain chairs all round the walls, on one end a large shining map, marked with all the colours of a rainbow.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as arid as a desert” most nearly suggests
options: a place made dangerous by heat and dust
a space that is bare and without warmth
a building located in a remote dry region
a stairway too steep and long to climb
items.explanation: 구절 바로 앞의 'swept and ungarnished'는 계단이 깨끗이 쓸렸지만 아무 장식도 없음을 보여 준다. 이어지는 평범한 의자, 우산 덮개 같은 옷차림 묘사도 삭막한 분위기를 이어 가므로 B가 정답이다. A와 C는 사막을 문자 그대로 받아들인 해석이다. D는 계단의 경사나 길이에 대한 언급이 없어 틀리다.

items.passage:
For I have published, be it confessed,
A little volume of verses,
And in the volume whatever is best
The praise of herself rehearses.

I sit by the fire, and again I dream
A happier dream than ever,
I see her beautiful eyes soft gleam
As she murmurs, "How lovely--how clever!"

Her criticism may be commonplace,
But who can be angry after
Now sweet with pity he marks her face,
Now bright with impulsive laughter?
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “A happier dream than ever” most nearly suggests
options: a nightmare about harsh reviews of the speaker's book
a plan to write a more successful volume of verses
a fond imagining of the woman's pleased response
a memory of a happier time before the book appeared
items.explanation: 화자는 난롯가에 앉아 꿈꾸면서 그녀의 눈이 부드럽게 빛나고 '정말 사랑스럽고 영리하다'고 속삭이는 모습을 본다. 앞 연에서 시집의 가장 좋은 부분이 그녀에 대한 찬사라고 했으므로, 이 꿈은 그녀가 기뻐하는 반응을 다정하게 상상하는 것이다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 반대 감정이고, B와 D는 새 계획이나 과거 회상에 대한 근거가 없다.

items.passage: One last word about our amiable author. His great book remains eminently alive, and wields after two centuries and a half a permanent influence. When you refer to it, you must not expect a logical development of philosophical theory. We do not look to find a system in a book of maxims and portraits. La Bruyere was a moralist, pure and simple; he awakened sensibility, he encouraged refinement, and he exposed the vicious difference which existed around him--and which no one else had seemed to notice--that the possession of more or fewer pieces of money made between human beings otherwise equal.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “eminently alive” most nearly suggests that the book
options: is filled with vivid scenes of physical action
describes its author's long and healthy life
was recently rediscovered after being lost
continues to be widely read and influential
items.explanation: 구절 바로 뒤에 이 책이 두 세기 반이 지난 뒤에도 '영구적인 영향력'을 행사한다는 설명이 이어진다. 따라서 '살아 있다'는 말은 책이 여전히 읽히고 영향력을 가진다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 이 책이 격언과 인물 묘사로 이루어졌다는 설명과 맞지 않는다. B는 '살아 있음'을 작가의 생애로 오해했고, C의 재발견은 언급되지 않는다.

items.passage: I took off its hat and cloak to see if there were any strings cutting its neck or choking it. Then I glanced at the feet, and lo! there was the trouble. The boots were at least one size too small. I took them off, and the stockings, too, and found the feet as cold as ice and the prints of the stockings clearly traced on the tender flesh. We all know the agony of tight boots. I rubbed the feet and held them in my hands until they were warm, when the poor little thing fell asleep.
items.question: As used in the text, the phrase “as cold as ice” most nearly suggests that the child's feet were
options: painfully chilled from poor circulation
unusually hard and stiff from walking
frozen solid after a winter accident
pale because the stockings were white
items.explanation: 화자는 신발이 한 치수 이상 작았고 발에 스타킹 자국이 깊게 남아 있었다고 말한다. 화자가 발을 문지르고 손으로 감싸 따뜻해지자 아이가 잠들었으므로, 이 구절은 꽉 끼는 신발 때문에 발이 몹시 차가워졌음을 나타낸다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 얼음의 단단함이나 색으로 잘못 해석한 것이다. C의 사고는 지문에 없다.

items.passage: The men who do the planting in summer find chopping to do in winter in the older plantations, at good wages. Money is flowing into the moor in the wake of the water and the marl. Roads are being made, and every day the mail-carrier comes. In the olden time a stranger straying into the heath often brought the first news of the world without for weeks together. Game is coming, too,—roebuck and deer,—in the young forests. The climate itself is changing; more rain falls in midsummer, when it is needed. The sand-blast has been ______, the power of the west wind broken. The shrivelled soil once more takes up and holds the rains, and the streams will deepen, fish leap in them as of yore.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: spread
checked
praised
measured
items.explanation: 빈칸 바로 뒤에서 서풍의 힘이 '꺾였다'고 하고, 이어 메마른 땅이 다시 빗물을 머금는다고 말한다. 글 전체가 황야가 회복되는 변화를 나열하므로 모래바람이 억제되었다는 뜻의 B가 정답이다. A는 상황이 악화되었다는 의미라 흐름과 반대이다. C와 D는 모래바람을 칭찬하거나 측정한다는 뜻으로 문맥에 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: What did such a whim as this mean? he asked himself, impatiently, taking in at a glance the new expression in her face, and the heaviness of her gloomy eyes. This was not one of her tricks. There was no one here to see her, and even if there had been, what end could she serve by crying over a letter from Pen’yllan? What, on earth, had she been crying for? He had never seen her shed a tear before in his life. He had often thought that such a thing was impossible, she was so ______. Could it be that she was not really so hard, after all, and that those three innocent old women could reach her heart?

items.explanation: 그는 그녀가 우는 것을 평생 본 적이 없어 그런 일은 불가능하다고 생각했다. 이어 마지막 문장에서 '결국 그녀가 그렇게 냉정하지 않은 것일까'라고 되묻는다. 따라서 빈칸에는 감정이 메마르고 단단하다는 뜻의 C가 들어간다. A, B, D는 눈물을 흘리지 않을 이유가 되지 않아 틀리다.

items.passage: Almost every article of home produce will command cash; but the merchant cannot get cash for his goods. Money is the representativ of goods bought and sold. I will suppose, for the sake of argument, that two years ago there was cash enough in the country to purchase all the goods in market at the usual advance. I will suppose that the quantity of goods has been ______ since that time. In this case, had the quantity of money continued the same, there would have been cash enough to purchase just one third of the goods. But suppose what is true, that at the time the quantity of goods increases in this proportion, the quantity of money in circulation diminishes in the same proportion.

items.explanation: 빈칸 다음 문장에서 돈의 양이 그대로라면 상품의 '정확히 3분의 1'만 살 수 있었을 것이라고 한다. 이는 상품의 양이 세 배가 되었다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. A는 상품이 줄었다는 뜻이라 3분의 1이라는 계산과 맞지 않는다. B와 C는 상품의 양을 바꾸는 말이 아니어서 다음 문장의 계산을 설명하지 못한다.

items.passage:
The two ______ of this suite of hers are the bed and bath-tub. The bed is on a raised platform in a sort of alcove. The canopy and curtains are of a wonderful shade of violet silk. The counter-pane and roll-cover are of costly lace. The head-board and foot-board are two splendid paintings--one of sleep, the other of awakening. You think nine thousand dollars was cheap for this bed, even without canopy, lace and other fineries.

The bath-tub is cut from a solid block of white marble and is sunk in the marble floor of her huge bathroom. It is a small swimming-pool, and its plumbing is silver, plated with gold. On the floor of this room at the step down into the tub there is a great white bear-skin, and there is another in front of the beautiful little dressing-table.

items.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에 이어지는 침대와 욕조 묘사는 보랏빛 비단, 값비싼 레이스, 금도금 은 배관 등 놀라운 사치품으로 가득하다. 따라서 두 물건을 '경이로운 것'으로 소개하는 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 부정적인 뜻이라 감탄하는 묘사와 반대이다. C는 두 물건이 자세히 설명되므로 수수께끼라고 할 수 없다.
